subtype: Approach: comparing free resources for study [Thinking]
passage:
Monday: Zeenat spread the coaching brochure on the table. The fee was more than her family could spare in a season. She wrote two columns: what coaching gives, and where else that could come from.

Wednesday: She tried the options one by one. The school library had past papers and reference books. The government video lessons explained integration in a way she could pause and replay. Urmila, a Class 12 senior, lent her neat notes in a binder. A study group of four met on Thursdays.

Saturday: Zeenat crossed out the brochure. Library on weekdays, videos for the hardest chapters, Urmila's notes to check her own, the Thursday group for doubts. "It won't be the same as coaching," she wrote, "but it fits what we have."

qa.q: How many people met in the Thursday study group?
qa.a: A study group of four met on Thursdays.

qa.q: What did Zeenat think about coaching and the free options, and how did that feel?
qa.a: Zeenat thought coaching was beyond what the family could spare, and felt practical and settled that the free mix would fit.

qa.q: What else could Zeenat add if a subject stays weak, and why?
qa.a: Zeenat could ask a teacher to check one weak topic every week, because a small dose of personal help fills a gap that free material leaves.

qa.q: How might Urmila see lending the notes?
qa.a: Urmila probably feels glad to pass on notes that are no longer needed, since sharing them helps a junior without cost.

grounding: Instead of buying expensive coaching, the teen weighs free options such as the school library, government video lessons, senior notes and a study group, and chooses those that fit best.

subtype: Approach: comparing free resources for study [Thinking]
passage: Harsha, you're upset you can't join that coaching centre? Listen to your Ramesh Mama. When I was preparing for my Class 12 exams, my family couldn't afford coaching either, and my friends were all going. I sat on the steps of the temple tank one evening and listed everything I could get free. The school library, open till five. Our Physics teacher, who stayed back for doubts on Wednesdays. My neighbour's son, a year senior, who still had his notes. The government's free lessons on television in the evening. And three friends who also weren't going to coaching. Then I asked myself which ones matched how I learn. Library and doubts for Physics. The senior's notes for Chemistry. A study group for Maths, because I learn by arguing. The television lessons I dropped. I passed with a first class.

qa.q: Which day did the Physics teacher stay back for doubts?
How might young Ramesh have felt when his friends all went to coaching?
qa.a: He probably felt left out and worried about falling behind, which pushed him to think carefully about his options.

qa.q: Which choice in the story shows good thinking, and why?
qa.a: Matching each free resource to how he learns, like the study group for Maths because he learns by arguing, and dropping what didn't fit.

qa.q: What might the study group have meant to the three friends?
qa.a: It gave them a group that fit their situation too, so none of them had to prepare alone without coaching.

grounding: An elder recalls weighing free study options instead of paid coaching and choosing those that fit how he learned.

subtype: Approach: comparing free resources for study [Thinking]
passage: Zeenat's friends were joining a coaching batch for the entrance exam, but at home there was no money for it this year, and the family phone had only a small data pack. So on Sunday she sat with a notebook and listed every free option she could find. The school library: open till six, quiet, with past papers. The government's free video lessons: excellent, but each one ate data. Omkar, a year senior, who had offered his handwritten notes. A study group with two girls from her lane. She thought about each one. Videos: download only the hard chapters on the library wifi and watch them offline at home. Notes: Chemistry, because Omkar's were famous. Library: every weekday. Group: Saturdays, for Maths problems. It wasn't coaching. But it was a plan that fit.

qa.q: Until what time is the school library open?
How might Zeenat have felt as her friends joined coaching?
qa.a: She probably felt left out and a little anxious, which pushed her to plan carefully instead.

qa.q: What makes Zeenat's plan for the videos clever?
qa.a: Downloading only the hard chapters on the library wifi and watching offline gets the best free lessons without using up the family's small data pack.

qa.q: How might Omkar feel about sharing his notes?
qa.a: Omkar may feel pleased and generous, glad his famous notes are helping a younger student.

grounding: Shows a teen with little money and data comparing free study resources and choosing the ones that fit best.
